title: Implement Magic Dictionary
description:
Design a data structure that is initialized with a list of distinct words. Provided a query string, you should determine if you can change **exactly one** character in this string to a different lowercase English letter so that it matches any string in the data structure.

Implement the `MagicDictionary` class:
- `MagicDictionary()` initializes the object.
- `void buildDict(String[] dictionary)` sets the data structure with an array of distinct strings `dictionary`.
- `boolean search(String searchWord)` returns `true` if you can change exactly one character in `searchWord` to match any string in the data structure, and `false` otherwise. Note that an exact match with zero changes does not count unless another dictionary word differs by exactly one character.
constraints: dictionary[i] consists of only lowercase English letters.
All strings in dictionary are distinct.
searchWord consists of only lowercase English letters.
buildDict is called once before search queries.
At most 100 calls will be made to search.
hints: Insert all dictionary words into a trie during buildDict.
For search(searchWord), run a DFS carrying the current character index, current trie node, and a boolean flag indicating whether the one allowed character modification has already been used.

If the modification has not been used yet, you may either follow the exact character (keeping modified = false) or follow any other existing child (setting modified = true). At the end of searchWord, return true only if modified is true and the node is a word end.

examples.explanation: "hello" requires 0 changes so it returns false; "hhllo" can change the second 'h' to 'e' to match "hello" (true); "hell" and "leetcoded" have wrong lengths (false).
Because both "hello" and "hallo" are in the dictionary, searching "hello" now returns true (change 'e' to 'a' to match "hallo").

timeComplexity: O(N * L) buildDict, O(26 * L^2) worst-case search
